AlreadyAddedResponse.description:
What the lookup may say about a number [BR2.3, BR4.5].

**Three fields, and the absences are the requirement.** No teacher
name, no teacher id, no batch name, no batch subject, no fee, no
enrollment id. With any of those this becomes an oracle for who
teaches whom, readable by anyone who can type a phone number
[AC1.12.2].

:ivar already_added: Whether a teacher recorded this number
:ivar display_name: The teacher-typed name to pre-fill as
    correctable, or None
:ivar role: The role to lock the form to, or None
AlreadyAddedResponse.title: AlreadyAddedResponse

BatchCreateRequest.description:
Create a batch [AC2.1.1, AC2.1.2].

:ivar name: The teacher's name for the class
:ivar subjects: One or more subjects taught
:ivar teacher_display_name: What students see the teacher called
:ivar default_fee: The fee an enrollment inherits when it sets none
:ivar fee_due_day: Day of month 1-31; 29-31 clamp at generation
:ivar collection_number: Where payments are sent
:ivar collection_channel: Which service that number belongs to

BatchResponse.description:
A batch as its owner sees it.

:ivar id: The batch
:ivar name: The teacher's name for the class
:ivar subjects: The subjects taught
:ivar teacher_display_name: What students see the teacher called
:ivar default_fee: The inherited fee
:ivar fee_due_day: Day of month 1-31
:ivar collection_number: Where payments are sent
:ivar collection_channel: Which service that number belongs to
:ivar marksheet_visible: U6's toggle
:ivar active: False means read-only history
:ivar enrollment_count: How many seats, computed server-side. The
    **denominator** of "9 of 12 accepted", and it counts every seat
    the teacher created including declined ones [BR1.4]
:ivar accepted_count: How many of those seats at least one link has
    accepted [BR1.2], computed server-side and **never counted by
    the client** [BR1.3, TC-9]. A client counting rows is a client
    deciding what counts as accepted, and it is wrong the moment the
    roster paginates because it can only count the rows it holds
BatchResponse.title: BatchResponse

ClaimResponse.description:
A claim and its decision, as its submitter sees it.

``previous_decision`` is carried deliberately: a corrected
verification is visible to the teacher **and** to that student and
guardian, never hidden from either party [BR5.7, FR9.2]. It is typed
as a map of strings because every value in it -- including the
amount -- is a string, so a money value inside it crosses the wire
under the same rule as every other [BR6.2].

:ivar claim_id: The claim
:ivar period: The period it resolved to at submission
:ivar claimed_amount: What was claimed
:ivar approved_amount: What was accepted, or null while pending
:ivar status: One of the four server-set values
:ivar shortfall_disposition: Carried or waived, where one applies
:ivar channel: Which service the money moved through
:ivar submitted_at: When it was submitted
:ivar verified_at: When it was decided, or null
:ivar previous_decision: The prior decision, on a correction
ClaimResponse.title: ClaimResponse

ClaimSubmitRequest.description:
Submit a payment claim [AC6.1.x].

``claimed_amount`` is **not capped** at the outstanding balance
[BR5.2]: money may genuinely have been overpaid out of band, and
blocking that at submission makes a real overpayment unreportable.
Zero and negative are refused, which the wire pattern already does
for a negative since it admits no sign.

:ivar claimed_amount: What the claimant says they paid
:ivar channel: Which service it moved through, from the server set
:ivar transaction_id: The reference they quote, if any
ClaimSubmitRequest.title: ClaimSubmitRequest

DecisionResponse.description:
The seat's state after this holder decided [BR5.2].

Reports **this holder's own** decision. The other link's state is
deliberately absent: it belongs to another person, and a seat whose
student and guardian are different people shows each state only to
its own holder. The teacher's roster is where both appear side by
side, and that screen is D2's [AC1.10.7].

:ivar enrollment_id: The seat decided on
:ivar decision: This holder's decision after the write
DecisionResponse.title: DecisionResponse

EnrollmentCreateRequest.description:
Add a student to a batch [AC2.2.2, AC2.2.5].

``fee_amount`` is nullable and null means **inherit** the batch
default. Zero is a real fee of zero, which is a waiver -- a
non-nullable column defaulting to zero would make the two
indistinguishable and silently charge nothing.

:ivar display_name: The teacher-typed name for this seat
:ivar student_phone: The student's number, typed by the teacher
:ivar guardian_phone: The guardian's number, if one is recorded
:ivar fee_amount: This seat's fee, or null to inherit
:ivar joined_on: When the student joined
EnrollmentCreateRequest.title: EnrollmentCreateRequest

GuardianChildResponse.description:
One reachable child as a guardian sees it.

Carries ``batch_name`` and ``teacher_display_name`` because
attribution is required even in the single-child case [AC2.8.5] --
that is where it is most needed, since the selection list is where
it would otherwise have been shown.

:ivar enrollment_id: The seat, which BR5.1 keys the route on
:ivar display_name: The teacher-typed name for the child
:ivar batch_name: Which class
:ivar teacher_display_name: Which teacher recorded this

What the smoke set reads.

:ivar status: ``ok`` when the process is serving
:ivar database: ``ok`` or ``fail``
:ivar migration_revision: The applied Alembic revision, or None

InactiveFromRequest.description:
Mark a seat inactive from a date, or clear it [AC2.4.1].

:ivar inactive_from: The date, or null to reactivate the seat
InactiveFromRequest.title: InactiveFromRequest

InvitationResponse.description:
One unaccepted seat, in exactly the width BR1.4 permits.

Batch name, subject and fee amount -- all teacher-authored, so this
read crosses no privacy boundary -- plus the seat's own id, which
the accept and decline routes are keyed on, and this holder's own
decision so the screen can offer the right action without deciding
what ``declined`` means for itself [TC-9].

**There is no attendance, no mark, no other enrollment and no
further batch field**, and no write action but accept and decline
on the link that names the holder [AC1.10.2].

:ivar enrollment_id: The seat, which the decision routes are keyed on
:ivar batch_name: The class being joined
:ivar subject: The subjects taught, as the teacher named them
:ivar fee_amount: This seat's fee, or None when it inherits the
    batch default. None is NOT zero: zero is a waiver
:ivar decision: This holder's own decision, ``pending`` or
    ``declined``
InvitationResponse.title: InvitationResponse

IssueRequest.description:
Ask for a code to be sent to a number.

The number is **typed by the user** and never read from the SIM
[AC1.1.6]: there is no device-side source for this field.

:ivar phone: The destination number in international form
IssueRequest.title: IssueRequest

IssueResponse.description:
The response to an issue request, for **any** number.

One field, and it is a fixed string. Anything varying between the
known and unknown branches -- a count, a timestamp, a message -- is
the existence oracle re-entering through the schema.

:ivar status: Always ``requested``
IssueResponse.title: IssueResponse

LensEntry.description:
One lens the account can choose.

:ivar kind: Which lens: teacher, student or guardian
:ivar count: How much sits behind it
LensEntry.title: LensEntry

MeResponse.description:
Everything this account can be.

**No role, and no default lens.** The list says what is available;
which one the person wants is their choice, and a server-chosen
default would be a stored role by another name. A single-entry
list is the app's cue to skip the picker.

:ivar lenses: Every available lens, teacher first
MeResponse.title: MeResponse

Money.description: A BDT amount in canonical form: exactly two decimal places, no thousands separator, no currency symbol, no sign. Always a JSON string, never a JSON number.
Money.title: Money

PaymentDestinationResponse.description:
Where to send a payment, and through what.

**The ONE response in the product carrying the collection number**
[BR6.4, NFR14.32]. The allowlist test asserts that as an equality
against a one-element set, so the field spreading to a second
response fails the build rather than passing a membership check.

Where the teacher set no number the route returns **no object at
all** rather than this model with a null in it [NFR14.34]: a null
invites a client-side placeholder, and an absent object leaves the
client nothing to render while the copy tells the person to ask the
teacher how to pay.

:ivar collection_number: Where payments are sent
:ivar collection_channel: Which service that number belongs to
:ivar channels: The channel set, server-supplied so adding one is a
    data change rather than an app release
PaymentDestinationResponse.title: PaymentDestinationResponse

RefreshRequest.description:
Present a refresh token for rotation.

:ivar refresh_token: The opaque token previously issued
RefreshRequest.title: RefreshRequest

RejectionRequest.description:
Reject a claim, optionally as a correction [BR5.6, BR5.7].

A body with one optional field rather than no body at all, because
rejection is correctable for the same reason approval is: a teacher
who rejected the wrong claim must be able to say so, and FR9.2 makes
no exception for the rejection path.

Every field defaults, so an ordinary rejection may still send no
body.

:ivar correcting: True when deliberately revising a decided claim
RejectionRequest.title: RejectionRequest

RosterFeeRowResponse.description:
One seat's fee position, as its teacher sees it.

The key is ``enrollment_id`` and never an account id [ADR-001],
asserted schema-wide by the built privacy gate.

**No ``collection_number``.** The teacher's payment destination is
carried by exactly one response and this is not it [NFR14.33].

:ivar enrollment_id: The teacher-facing key
:ivar display_name: The teacher-typed name
:ivar outstanding: What this seat owes across every period
:ivar current_period: The latest generated period, or null
:ivar current_status: That period's status, or null
:ivar due_date: That period's due date, or null
RosterFeeRowResponse.title: RosterFeeRowResponse

RosterRowResponse.description:
One seat as a teacher sees it.

``status`` is a **server-computed decision**, not an input to one
[TC-9]: the client switches on this enum and never compares a date
or an amount of its own.

:ivar enrollment_id: The teacher-facing key for this seat
:ivar display_name: The teacher-typed name
:ivar guardian_phone: The teacher-typed guardian contact
:ivar fee_amount: This seat's fee, or null when it inherits
:ivar status: ``dormant``, ``active`` or ``inactive``.

    **Unchanged, and the two new fields sit beside it rather than
    replacing it.** Acceptance is a different axis from activity:
    an inactive seat keeps whatever decisions its links carry,
    because leaving a batch is not un-accepting it. Folding the two
    together would produce a product of two axes and a value set
    nobody can switch on exhaustively
:ivar student_state: The student link's own decision --
    ``pending``, ``accepted`` or ``declined`` [BR2.1]
:ivar guardian_state: The guardian link's own decision, plus
    ``absent`` when no guardian was recorded [BR2.2]. ``absent`` is
    a fourth VALUE and not a null, because a decision nobody was
    asked for is not an outstanding one
:ivar is_removable: Whether removal would succeed [BR3.1].

    **A decision the client reads and never derives** [NFR14.31].
    Removal tests two conditions -- no link accepted, and no erasure
    marker set -- and this row carries only the first. A client
    inferring removability from the link states it displays would
    offer the action on an erased seat, which is a wrong answer
    presented as an available action rather than a style violation
:ivar inactive_from: The recorded date, if any
RosterRowResponse.title: RosterRowResponse

SignupRequest.description:
Create an account for a number nobody has registered.

The number is **typed by the person** and never read from the SIM
[TC-4, D-35]: there is no device-side source for this field, here
or anywhere in this product.

:ivar phone: The number this identity is keyed on
:ivar role: The claimed role; nothing verifies it [BR4.2]
:ivar self_name: The name the person chose for themselves. Lands on
    ``Profile.self_name`` and never on an ``Enrollment.display_name``
    [BR3.1]
:ivar address: Owner-private, and optional because the
    already-added path reaches signup with no address yet
SignupRequest.title: SignupRequest

SignupResponse.description:
The account exists and a code is on its way [BR4.3].

**No token and no lens.** The account is created before the code is
sent, and the person is authenticated by the existing OTP flow,
unchanged [BR2.2]. Returning a token here would make signup a
second authentication path with none of the seven controls the
first one carries.

:ivar account_id: The new account
:ivar code_sent_to: The number the code was sent to, echoed so the
    screen can name its destination [BR4.3, AC1.11.4]
SignupResponse.title: SignupResponse

TokenResponse.description:
A freshly issued token pair.

**No lens and no role here either.** The response says nothing about
what the account may do; that is resolved per request from the data
[BR1.1].

:ivar access_token: The short-lived bearer token
:ivar refresh_token: The long-lived rotation token
:ivar expires_in: Access-token lifetime in seconds
TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse

VerificationRequest.description:
Record a teacher's decision on a claim [AC6.3.x].

``shortfall_disposition`` is **required where the approval is below
the charge and forbidden where it is not** [BR5.4]. It carries no
default: the two choices have opposite consequences for the student,
so a default silently chooses for the teacher. The requirement
cannot be expressed in the schema alone -- it depends on what the
cycle was charged -- so the server enforces it and this field stays
optional here.

``correcting`` is **the teacher saying "I know this claim is already
decided and I am revising it"** [BR5.7, FR9.2]. It defaults to
``False``, so an ordinary verification of an undecided claim needs no
flag and a *concurrent* second verification is refused rather than
silently double-crediting the payment.

It cannot be inferred from the claim's state. A decided claim with a
second request arriving is exactly the shape of both the race this
guard exists to stop and the correction FR9.2 requires, and the
server cannot tell them apart -- only the teacher knows which one
they meant. Inferring it would mean choosing to let the race through.

:ivar approved_amount: What the teacher accepts
:ivar shortfall_disposition: Carried or waived, where one applies
:ivar correcting: True when deliberately revising a decided claim
VerificationRequest.title: VerificationRequest

VerifyRequest.description:
Present a code for verification.

:ivar phone: The number the code was issued for
:ivar code: The six-digit code
VerifyRequest.title: VerifyRequest

post.description:
Create an account, then send the verification code [BR4.3].

**The ordering is the requirement, not an implementation detail**
[AC1.11.4]. The account exists before the code is sent, so a person
who verifies always has something to verify into; sending first
would mean a code arriving for an account that may never be
created.

The ceiling is consumed **before** the account is created, for the
reason the OTP path checks before its gateway call: a ceiling
checked afterwards has already spent what it exists to protect.

Public by design, and in ``PUBLIC_ROUTES``: there is no session to
authenticate with before an account exists.

:param body: The signup request
:param request: The incoming request
:param session: The request-scoped session
:param gateway: The configured SMS gateway
:return: The new account and the number its code went to
:raises CeilingBreach: A signup ceiling refused this request
:raises DuplicateNumber: The number already has an account

get.description:
Report whether a teacher recorded this number, and nothing more.

**This route discloses that a seat exists, deliberately**
[BR2.3, AC1.12.2]. That is its purpose, and it is why BR2.2's
byte-identical requirement applies to the OTP endpoint and not to
this one. What is bounded is the WIDTH -- never the teacher, never
the batch -- and the rate, through signup's own ceilings.

Public, and in ``PUBLIC_ROUTES``: it is called while the signup
form renders, before any account exists.

:param phone: The number typed into the form
:param request: The incoming request
:param session: The request-scoped session
:return: Existence, the name to pre-fill and the role to lock
:raises CeilingBreach: A signup ceiling refused this request

List every unaccepted seat this account holds [BR1.3, BR5.5].

**Lens-exempt for the same reason ``GET /v1/me`` is**, and recorded
in ``LENS_EXEMPT_AUTHENTICATED`` rather than left to infer: this is
the route that REPORTS which invitation lenses exist, so requiring
one would mean a person had to already know which seats they were
offered in order to ask. Every row it returns is derived from the
authenticated account id and it reads nothing another account could
own.

A **declined** seat stays in this list with its state, because its
holder may change their mind [BR5.4, AC1.13.1]. A seat whose links
this account holds BOTH appears once [BR5.3].

post.description:
Accept this seat, from ``pending`` or from ``declined``.

One route for both, because accepting after a decline is the same
operation and not a second one [BR5.4, AC1.13.2]: the lens becomes
available exactly as if the person had accepted first time.

:param lens: The invitation lens carrying the one reachable seat
:param session: The request-scoped session
:return: The seat and this holder's decision

Decline this seat, withdrawing only this holder's own lens.

**A guardian's decline does not stop the student's fee** [BR5.2,
